assessments.reasoning: GNU FTP lines 134–136, bytes [6963,7173), cover the Program or a covered work based on it in object-code or executable form. The opening requires an additional §3 alternative alongside the applicable §§1–2 terms. Reading §3(a)'s source-accompaniment alternative confirms that failing §3(c) alone does not decide the other routes.

GNU FTP lines 142–153, bytes [7392,8100), require a written §3(b) offer valid for at least three years, open to any third party, at no more than the physical cost of source distribution. It covers complete machine-readable corresponding source under §§1–2 on a customary software-interchange medium. Section 3(c) expressly incorporates those offer terms and requires noncommercial redistribution with the information received about that offer.

limitations: The finding concerns the §3(c) route. Sections 3(a) and 3(b) provide separate alternatives. Actual distribution and receipt conditions require transaction-specific evidence.
reasoning: Under GPL version 2, §3(c) allows a noncommercial redistributor who received object code or an executable with a qualifying §3(b) offer to pass on the binary accompanied by the received offer information. Sections 1 and 2 continue to apply as specified by §3.
